name: Mutation Testing
tagline: Measuring test suite strength by injecting small syntactic bugs ('mutants') and verifying that tests fail.
purpose: Expose weak assertions hidden behind 95%+ line coverage using diff-scoped mutation testing (PITest, Stryker, mutmut).

spark.summary: Mutation testing evaluates the quality of your test suite by automatically injecting tiny bugs ('mutants')—like flipping `>` to `>=` or removing a return value—into production code and checking whether your tests fail.
spark.keyTakeaway: If latency budgets leave no room for synchronous retries, code coverage measures which lines were executed, not whether assertions actually check correctness; run diff-scoped mutation testing on critical business logic (pricing, auth, state machines) to achieve an 80–90% mutation score.
spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** **Mutation testing** (PITest for Java, Stryker for TS/C#, `mutmut` for Python) injects single syntactic faults—**mutants**—such as flipping `+` to `-`, `>` to `>=`, `true` to `false`, or `&&` to `||` into compiled bytecode or the AST, then runs covering tests.

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts AST/Bytecode Mutant Generation & Test Verification (INJECT MUTANT -> KILLED -> SURVIVED); PR Diff -> Coverage Map -> Incremental Mutant Run (PR Diff -> Per-Test Coverage -> Stryker / PITest -> CI Gate (>=75%)).

**Trade-Offs & Production:** Combine fast PR diff mutation with property-based testing for complementary bug discovery. Mature engineering orgs run `perTest` coverage-filtered incremental mutation on PRs touching `pricing/`, `billing/`, or `auth/` (blocking merges below 75%), and execute a.

**Failure Modes & Application:** Connect mutation testing to property-based testing, test doubles, and CI/CD quality gates.

learningJourney.title: What is Mutation Testing

explanation.foundation: **Mutation testing** (PITest for Java, Stryker for TS/C#, `mutmut` for Python) injects single syntactic faults—**mutants**—such as flipping `+` to `-`, `>` to `>=`, `true` to `false`, or `&&` to `||` into compiled bytecode or the AST, then runs covering tests.
explanation.core: Outcomes fall into four buckets: **Killed** (test failed—good!), **Survived** (tests still passed—assertion gap!), **Timed Out** (infinite loop—killed), and **No Coverage**. **Mutation Score** = `Killed / (Total - Equivalent)`.

learningJourney.title: Why 95% line coverage gives false confidence

explanation.foundation: A test suite can hit 95% line coverage while having weak or tautological assertions—executing a discount calculation without ever asserting the final price.
explanation.core: Two operational traps deter teams: **CI Timeout Explosion** (running 15,000 mutants across a 100k-line repo without coverage filtering) and **Equivalent Mutant Fatigue** (burning hours on a mutant that is semantically identical to the original code, like a cache-shortcut check).

decisionFramework.problem: How to implement Mutation Testing without hitting unbounded tail latency, state divergence, or operational fragility.
decisionFramework.naiveSolution: Use a single unpartitioned path with unbounded retries and synchronous global coordination.
decisionFramework.whyItFails: Global coordination serializes throughput under load, while unbounded retries amplify transient stalls into full outages.
decisionFramework.alternatives: Compare synchronous strict-consistency paths against bounded asynchronous replication, local caching, or partitioned ownership.
decisionFramework.decision: If latency budgets leave no room for synchronous retries, code coverage measures which lines were executed, not whether assertions actually check correctness; run diff-scoped mutation testing on critical business logic (pricing, auth, state machines) to achieve an 80–90% mutation score.
decisionFramework.tradeOffs: Gains predictable p99 latency and fault isolation in exchange for explicit bounding, observability, and slightly higher implementation complexity.

options.text: The production code has a syntax error
options.feedback: Mutants that fail to compile are discarded, not counted as survived.

options.text: A deliberate bug was injected into covered code and all tests still passed, exposing a weak or missing assertion
options.feedback: Correct: surviving mutants reveal blind spots where line coverage gave false confidence.

options.text: The test suite ran too slowly
options.feedback: Slow infinite-loop mutants are marked as Timed Out (killed).
